chapter: New Orleans clarinetists and Steve Lewis
title: Favorite clarinet players: Joe Watson, Zib, Blind Freddy
summary: Handy names the clarinetists he admired in New Orleans and a reading man who played only with Piron's band and never sat in.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, who were some of the best clarinet players in New Orleans when you first came here?
Oh, when I first came here, I liked it, uh, Joe Watson with Sam Morgan.

I liked it, him for clarinet. Mm-hmm. And then I had another fellow, I liked it pretty good, played with Rene, called him Zib. Oh, yeah. Yeah, he was a nice clarinet player. Mm-hmm. And then I had this fellow, Blind Freddy. Mm-hmm. Wonderful. He could play about as much clarinet with one piece of it, he's the average guy to play with the whole horn. Mm-hmm. And he was a wonderful harmonica player, too. I think he still plays, I don't know.

He maybe do, but I haven't seen him play in a long time. Matter of fact, I haven't heard him play anything in a long time. I run across him every night, and then, yeah, he passes by my house. Mm-hmm. And then I had this fellow, T.O. used to play a lot of clarinet, too, with P. Ron. But he was mostly a reading man, to sit out and play that music.
Well, how did he do if he got in some Barrel House place and had to cut loose? Suppose he...
He would never sit in with a band? No.

I never was going to go, no. Never would get him sit in with a body. Played strictly with P. Ron. And after he finished that, that's it all. Matter of fact, he'd go home, he would never come around us, no way. Mm-hmm. No, unless he was passing there, and the rest of the band stopped there for, listened for a while. He might stand up there and listen, but he soon disappeared, he'd go.
